subject: Retention boundary check — enterprise audit examples and deletion path
body:
From: Sam Kapoor <sam.kapoor@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme Health Security Team <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Retention question for upcoming audit — prompts vs outputs

Hi Kimberly,

We’re preparing for our audit next month and want to confirm what Redwood stores by default. Specifically: when our product makes a call to the Redwood API, which of the following are considered "stored logs" by default?

- Raw user prompt (the text the user typed)
- Model-generated text (the output the model returned)
- Request/response metadata (latency, model version, token counts)

We found different references in the docs and want a short, audit-friendly explanation and an example that we can include in our evidence packet. Also, do you have a deletion path if we request a purge for a specific customer session?

Thanks — Sam
Security Lead, Acme Health

---

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sam Kapoor <sam.kapoor@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention question for upcoming audit — prompts vs outputs

Hi Sam — thanks for sending this over and for the heads-up on the audit. Short answer up front: by default Redwood stores request/response artifacts for telemetry and product diagnostics, but the policy distinguishes between ephemeral model-decoded content and persisted artifacts depending on customer settings and deployment mode. Below is an audit-friendly breakdown and an example.

Default behavior (hosted API) — concise audit summary:
- Prompts (raw user input): persisted by default as a request artifact unless you enable prompt redaction or opt out via the retention API. These are indexed for debugging and quality monitoring.
- Model outputs: stored by default as part of the response artifact, but can be configured to be non-persistent (ephemeral) for customers with stricter privacy requirements.
- Telemetry/metadata: latency, token usage, model_id, and sequence lengths are stored by default and are retained separately from full content.

Example (what would appear in an evidence export):
- request_id: r_12345
- timestamp: 2027-04-01T14:22:05Z
- prompt_snippet: "Patient reported headache for last 3 days..." (full prompt included unless redaction enabled)
- model_id: gpt-redwood-11b-v1
- response_snippet: "Recommend OTC analgesics and follow-up in 48 hours."
- tokens_request: 48, tokens_response: 27

Deletion path (customer-initiated purge):
1) Submit a purge request (API or Console) scoped to customer_id / session_id / request_id.
2) Purge job is scheduled; content artifacts are removed from the primary store and pointers are marked for deletion.
3) Backups: snapshots are retained per our backup policy; we perform an expunge cycle that removes purged items in the next retention sweep (typical window: up to 30 days for hosted backups). For Dedicated/Private customers, backup windows follow the customer’s contract.

I’m attaching a short retention matrix and a sample export you can include in your packet.

Action items:
- If you want zero persistence of prompts/outputs, request prompt_redaction=true and ephemeral_responses=true; we’ll send a config example.
- For an immediate purge, send the session_id(s) and we’ll kick off the purge job and provide the job id / audit trail.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

> Thanks Kimberly — that helps. A couple follow-ups:

> 2) If we enable prompt_redaction=true and ephemeral_responses=true at account level, will any artifacts still be written to logs for billing/debugging (e.g., token counts or a hashed placeholder)? We need to keep billing integrity but avoid storing plaintext prompts/outputs.
>

>

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sam Kapoor <sam.kapoor@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Acme Health Security Team <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Apr 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention question for upcoming audit — prompts vs outputs

Sam — answering directly:

1) Expunge timeline: for hosted customers we guarantee that purged artifacts are removed from live stores immediately and will be unrecoverable from primary stores. Backup snapshots are handled on a 30-day rolling expunge schedule for the hosted plan (so in the worst case, artifacts may persist in backups up to 30 days post-purge).
- If your compliance requirement is 45 days, we can: (a) perform an accelerated expunge and provide a signed attestation once the backup sweep completes, or (b) recommend Dedicated/Private deployment where backup windows are contractually customizable.

2) Billing & debugging telemetry when redaction is enabled:
- We still capture anonymized telemetry: token counts, model_id, latency, and a request hash (SHA256) that cannot be reversed to plaintext.
- No plaintext prompts or model outputs will be written to persistent logs when prompt_redaction=true and ephemeral_responses=true. We can provide a sample billing record format for your finance team.

Next steps I can take this afternoon:
- Provision account-level config example for prompt_redaction and ephemeral responses and share a one-page JSON snippet for your engineers.
- Kick off a purge job if you send the session_ids; I will cc Infra so you receive the purge job id and audit trail.

Please confirm which option you prefer for the expunge attestation (accelerated expunge + attestation vs Dedicated plan discussion).

Thanks — I’ve uploaded the retention matrix and a sample audit export to the Drive link and attached the intake form back for reference.

—Kimberly
